question: Combining Figure 5 (Page 8) and Table 13 (Page 33), what 3-shot MMLU accuracy does GPT-4 achieve in Latvian and Welsh, and what are the approximate speaker populations listed for those two languages in Table 13?
expected_answer: From Figure 5 (Page 8), GPT-4 achieves 80.9% 3-shot MMLU accuracy in Latvian and 77.5% in Welsh (both outperforming GPT-3.5 English at 70.1%). From Table 13 (Page 33), Latvian has approximately 2M speakers and Welsh has approximately 600k speakers.

gold.unit_and_condition: Speaker population counts in Table 13 on Page 33.

answer: GPT‑4 achieves a 3‑shot MMLU accuracy of **80.9 %** on Latvian and **77.5 %** on Welsh [gpt4-2023-techreport_p008_chart_01]. Table 13 lists the approximate speaker populations as **2 million** for Latvian and **600 000** for Welsh [gpt4-2023-techreport_p033_table_01].

We translated all questions and answers from MMLU [49] using Azure Translate. We used an external model to perform the translation, instead of relying on GPT-4 itself, in case the model had unrepresentative performance for its own translations. We selected a range of languages that cover different geographic regions and scripts, we show an example question taken from the astronomy category translated into Marathi, Latvian and Welsh in Table 13. The translations are not perfect, in some cases losing subtle information which may hurt performance. Furthermore some translations preserve proper nouns in English, as per translation conventions, which may aid performance.

Many existing ML benchmarks are written in English. To gain an initial understanding of GPT-4’s capabilities in other languages, we translated the MMLU benchmark [35, 36] – a suite of multiple- choice problems spanning 57 subjects – into a variety of languages using Azure Translate (see Appendix F for example translations and prompts). We find that GPT-4 outperforms the English- language performance of GPT 3.5 and existing language models (Chinchilla [2] and PaLM [3]) for the majority of languages we tested, including low-resource languages such as Latvian, Welsh, and Swahili (Figure 5).

Table 2: Performance of GPT-4 on traditional academic benchmarks (Columns: Benchmark | GPT-4 | GPT-3.5 | LM SOTA few-shot | Best external SOTA incl. benchmark-specific tuning):
- MMLU (57 subjects): GPT-4 (5-shot) = 86.4%; GPT-3.5 (5-shot) = 70.0%; LM SOTA (5-shot U-PaLM) = 70.7%; SOTA (5-shot Flan-PaLM) = 75.2%.
- HellaSwag: GPT-4 (10-shot) = 95.3%; GPT-3.5 (10-shot) = 85.5%; LM SOTA (LLaMA val) = 84.2%; SOTA (ALUM) = 85.6%.
- AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC Challenge-set): GPT-4 (25-shot) = 96.3%; GPT-3.5 (25-shot) = 85.2%; LM SOTA (8-shot PaLM) = 85.2%; SOTA (ST-MOE) = 86.5%.
- WinoGrande: GPT-4 (5-shot) = 87.5%; GPT-3.5 (5-shot) = 81.6%; LM SOTA (5-shot PaLM) = 85.1%; SOTA = 85.1%.
- HumanEval (Python coding): GPT-4 (0-shot) = 67.0%; GPT-3.5 (0-shot) = 48.1%; LM SOTA (0-shot PaLM) = 26.2%; SOTA (CodeT + GPT-3.5) = 65.8%.
- DROP (F1 score, reading comprehension & arithmetic): GPT-4 (3-shot) = 80.9; GPT-3.5 (3-shot) = 64.1; LM SOTA (1-shot PaLM) = 70.8; SOTA (QDGAT) = 88.4. (DROP is the only dataset in Table 2 where GPT-4 does not beat benchmark-specific SOTA).
- GSM-8K (grade-school math): GPT-4 (5-shot chain-of-thought, part of training set in pre-training mix) = 92.0%; GPT-3.5 (5-shot) = 57.1%; LM SOTA (8-shot Minerva) = 58.8%; SOTA (Chinchilla + SFT + ORM-RL) = 87.3%.

GPT-4 accepts prompts consisting of both images and text, which – parallel to the text-only setting – lets the user specify any vision or language task. Specifically, the model generates text outputs given inputs consisting of arbitrarily interlaced text and images. Over a range of domains – including documents with text and photographs, diagrams, or screenshots – GPT-4 exhibits similar capabilities as it does on text-only inputs. An example of GPT-4’s visual input can be found in Table 3. The standard test-time techniques developed for language models (e.g. few-shot prompting, chain-of- thought, etc) are similarly effective when using both images and text - see Appendix G for examples.
